idiom_name: tagged struct (enum discriminator + union payload) + handler table over a message queue
implementation_notes: ISO C has neither a message type nor dynamic dispatch, so the classic structure is written by hand: a struct holding an enum tag plus a union of parameter structs, framed and serialized explicitly, and delivered over a POSIX message queue (mq_send/mq_receive) or a Unix-domain socket. The receiver switches on the tag (or indexes a function-pointer table) and calls the single handler that owns the state - this hand-rolled dispatch table replaces the command class hierarchy, and the tag validation replaces the type system. There is no library shortcut worth taking here; the pattern in C is always this explicit.
pitfalls: Only the union member whose tag was written may be read - reading another member is undefined behaviour (C17 6.7.2.1), so the tag must be validated before any payload access.
A raw struct is not a wire format: padding, alignment and endianness differ between compilers and hosts, so a received command has to be parsed field by field rather than memcpy'd into the struct.
Indexing a handler table with an unvalidated tag reads outside the array; bound-check the discriminator and route unknown tags to an error path.
